key_concepts: The course is made of six chapters:
Tips you should know before you start rigging
Rigify fundamentals: how it works, its UI, how to break it, and how to fix it
Exploring each rig type in depth: how they work and how to improve them
Advanced Rigify workflow techniques like the use of postscripts or the action manager
Finally, rigging the Crimson Ronin, the character model included in the course

content: Go to [k]Edit > Prefences[/k] (Image 1) and then [k]Add-Ons[/k] (Image 2). Rigify is installed by default in Blender, search for 'rigify' and then enable it (Image 3). You should also review the [url]Rigify Documentation^^https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/addons/rigify/[/url].
Go to [k]Prefences > Get Extensions[/k] and search for and install 'icon viewer' (Image 6). This allows you to see the name of each icon in Blender.

The last add-on to install is 'bone widget' (Image 7). Bone Widget is a blender add-on to assist with making custom bone shapes. It has an editable library of shapes that make it easy to apply to any rig.
You only need basic Python scripting knowledge to understand the scripts provided in the course. And it’s much better to use them when you actually know what you’re reading.
Adding constraints, duplicating bones, editing influences... requires only low-level Python skills and will drastically improve your rigging abilities
